title: Flow Tracer: follow one payment from link to ledger
briefing: You are watching one payment travel through the platform. Nothing here is real. Your job: put the steps in order, and spot where the platform refuses to trust the browser.

tasks.title: Order the life of a payment
tasks.prompt: Put these steps in the order they happen.

items.label: The platform guards check the merchant, limits and rules
A slot is reserved on the link
The engine starts the payment with the partner
The customer completes the payment with the partner
Our server verifies the result with the partner
Success and the ledger entry are written in one transaction

tasks.feedback: Guards run first, the slot is reserved before any attempt, and success and posting are one transaction.

tasks.title: A tampered amount
tasks.prompt: The web address shows an amount of 1.000. What does the platform do?

options.label: Charges 1.000 because the customer asked for it
options.feedback: The amount never comes from the browser.

options.label: Ignores it and uses the link's amount from its own database
options.feedback: Correct. Amounts come only from the system.

options.label: Asks the merchant to confirm 1.000
options.feedback: There is nothing to confirm; the browser is not a source of amounts.

tasks.title: A tampered return address

panels.title: The customer's browser comes back from the partner's page
rows: Our server's own check with the partner

tasks.prompt: The return address says success. What do we do?

options.label: Mark the payment SUCCEEDED
options.feedback: A return address is only a hint and can be changed by anyone.

options.label: Ask the partner what really happened, and wait for its answer
options.feedback: Correct. Hints make us ask; only verified answers count.

options.label: Mark it FAILED because it is unverified
options.feedback: Unverified is not failed. We ask.

tasks.title: Which proof counts?

rows: A screenshot of a Paid screen
A signed webhook that passes all checks and matches reference, amount, currency, environment
A phone call from the customer

tasks.prompt: Which one can make the payment SUCCEEDED?

options.label: The verified signed webhook
options.feedback: Correct, if the five facts match.

tasks.title: Where does the money get written?
tasks.prompt: When is the ledger entry written?

options.label: In the same database transaction as the success
options.feedback: Correct. There is no state where a payment is SUCCEEDED without its entry.

options.label: Tomorrow morning in a batch
options.feedback: Success and posting are one transaction.

options.label: When Finance clicks a button
options.feedback: Finance does not post ordinary payments.

title: Approval Desk: be the checker
briefing: You are the checker. Four requests are waiting. For each, decide whether to **Approve** or **Reject** and choose the reason that would survive an audit. You are the second pair of eyes: if you do not understand a request, you do not approve it.

panels.title: Request
rows: Merchant request in portal; bank letter attached; old account closed. Letter checked: holder matches legal name.

options.label: **Approve**: the reason is specific and the holder matches
options.feedback: Correct. The reason says what was checked and the holder matches the legal name.

options.label: **Reject**: bank changes are always rejected
options.feedback: Legitimate changes exist; reject only when you cannot support the change.

options.label: **Approve** without opening **Review**
options.feedback: You must read the old and new value yourself.

panels.title: A colleague says
panels.text: "Just click Approve for me, I am busy and it is obviously fine."

options.label: Approve it to help
options.feedback: You made it. Approving your own work, or asking someone else to, defeats the control.

options.label: Refuse: the system will not let you, and a second person must review it properly
options.feedback: Correct. Ask a different checker to read it.

options.label: Ask the colleague to click Approve from your account
options.feedback: Sharing your account is a serious breach.

panels.title: Request
rows: This record changed after the request was made

options.label: **Reject** with a reason: the record changed; ask the maker to create a new request from the current values
options.feedback: Correct. Stale requests are never applied.

options.label: **Approve** because the new value looks fine
options.feedback: The request may overwrite changes it never saw.

panels.title: You decided to reject the request in the last task.
panels.text: Choose the reason you will type in **Decision reason**.

options.label: "no"
options.feedback: A reason must say what you checked and why.

options.label: "Record changed since request (v12 vs v14). Maker to re-submit from current values."
"compliance flagged this merchant"
options.feedback: Never reveal AML or compliance matters in a reason a merchant might read.

tasks.title: The safeguard checklist

panels.title: You are about to approve a 250.000 LYD refund.
rows: Duplicate charge; customer paid twice; first payment verified in the step log

tasks.prompt: Tick only the statements you have really verified from this record.

items.label: I read the old and new value in **Review**
items.why: You have this record in front of you.

items.label: The amount and currency match the original payment
The maker's reason makes sense
items.why: It names the duplicate and the evidence.

items.label: The environment badge is LIVE
I confirmed the customer's identity by phone
items.why: Nothing in the record supports this; do not tick what you did not do.

items.label: The maker is a different person from me
items.why: Stated in the request (you are the checker).

title: Security Desk: spot the trick
briefing: Six messages arrive during your shift. For each, choose the safe response.

panels.title: Phone call
panels.text: "Hi, this is Karim from IT. We are fixing a login fault. Please read me the code on your phone so I can finish the repair."

options.label: Read the code; he is from IT
options.feedback: Nobody legitimate ever asks for a code.

options.label: Refuse, end the call, and report it to the Security Admin
Read half the code
options.feedback: Never share any part of it.

panels.title: Email
panels.text: "URGENT from the CEO: process this payout today and do not discuss it with anyone. Details in the link below."

options.label: Click the link and process it
options.feedback: Urgency plus secrecy is a classic trick.

options.label: Do not click; use the normal screens and verify through a number you already know; report it
Forward it to the team
options.feedback: Do not spread it; report it to Security.

panels.title: Team chat
panels.text: A colleague posts a screenshot of a merchant's API token by mistake and asks if anyone saw it.

options.label: Say nothing
options.feedback: A leaked secret is usable until replaced.

options.label: Tell the Security Admin immediately; the merchant revokes and replaces the token
Delete the message and hope
options.feedback: Deleting does not unleak a secret.

panels.title: A merchant's owner says
panels.text: "If you approve my cash-out today I will send you a nice gift."

options.label: Decline, process nothing outside the normal checks, and report the offer
Accept and wait until after approval

tasks.title: What is safe to put in team chat?

panels.title: You need help from a colleague on one payment.

tasks.prompt: Tick only what you may safely send.

items.label: The payment reference
The customer's full phone number
items.why: Do not share personal data in chat.

items.label: The merchant's API token
A screenshot that shows a one-time code
The status you read in the platform

panels.title: What you noticed
panels.text: Two merchants share the same owner phone number and uploaded the same registry certificate, and one of them asks you what amount triggers a review.

options.label: Tell them the threshold
options.feedback: That reveals how to avoid detection and may tip them off.

title: KYB Desk: review five join requests
briefing: You review join requests. For each, choose the right action. Remember: never tell an applicant about screening, and a second reviewer is required in the cases the policy lists.

panels.title: Join request JR-1001
rows: 2 declared, both with ID; articles confirm 60/40

options.label: **Approve**
options.feedback: All seven checks pass and no second-person trigger fired.

options.label: **Reject** for safety
options.feedback: There is no reason to reject.

options.label: **Request information**: ask for a bank letter in the merchant's legal name
options.feedback: A mismatched payout account fails check 6 and forces a second reviewer; ask for the right letter.

options.label: Approve; the names are similar
options.feedback: A payout account must belong to the business (or a documented related party).

options.label: Reject and say screening found an issue
options.feedback: False and forbidden: never mention screening.

panels.title: Join request JR-1003
rows: Identical to a file uploaded by Bright Star LLC

options.label: Accuse the applicant of fraud
options.feedback: A duplicate does not reject automatically and you do not accuse.

options.label: Note the finding, review the related records, require a second reviewer and escalate to Compliance
options.feedback: Correct. The duplicate flag adds review and raises the proposed tier.

options.label: Approve; documents are just files
options.feedback: A duplicate is a serious warning sign.

tasks.prompt: You are an operator. What do you do?

options.label: Do not approve and do not discuss it; note it is waiting for Compliance and let the second-reviewer rule work
Approve because it is probably a false positive
Tell the applicant to explain the match
options.feedback: Never discuss screening with the applicant.

tasks.title: Which findings force a second reviewer? (risk-based policy)
tasks.prompt: Select all that force a second reviewer.

options.label: The payout account does not match

Mark it failed because it is 40 minutes old
Re-send the OTP

title: Incident Simulator: a switch timeout
briefing: A national switch had a timeout. Three payments are UNKNOWN and one webhook disagrees with an inquiry. Resolve each safely without double-crediting.

options.label: Confirm the breaker and tell the Gateway Admin and your manager
Re-enable the route
options.feedback: Never while the partner is failing.

options.label: Press **Inquire** once and read the step log
options.feedback: Correct; the platform resolves it if the partner answers clearly.

options.label: Leave the case open, note references, wait for the statement or evidence from the partner
Ask the customer to pay again

panels.title: U3
rows: Partner support replied in writing: payment completed, provider reference matches ours, amount and currency match

options.label: Use **Resolve as succeeded** with a reason naming the evidence, with a second person approving
Escalate to a senior operator and the Gateway Admin; resolution needs partner evidence
Resolve as succeeded because the webhook is signed
options.feedback: Both sources are trusted; neither wins.

tasks.title: After the breaker closes

items.label: Check the Unknown Backlog tile
Run Bulk Inquiry on the affected route and period using the checklist
Resolve remaining cases only with evidence and a second person
Write a handover note

tasks.feedback: Backlog first, then targeted inquiry, then evidence-based resolution, then hand over.

"We are confirming with your provider. Please do not pay again. We will update you."

title: Ledger Balancing Lab
briefing: Build the journal lines yourself. Enter debit or credit amounts (four decimals not needed) for the accounts that move; leave the others empty. Every entry must balance. Use 100.000 LYD links, 3% commission, and the fees given.

tasks.title: Entry 5: payer surcharge
tasks.prompt: Post the confirmation. The customer pays link plus commission; the merchant is credited the full link amount.
tasks.feedback: Clearing 103.0000 and fee expense 0.8000 on the debit side; wallet 100.0000, income 3.0000 and fee accrual 0.8000 on the credit side. Both sides total 103.8000.

tasks.title: Entry 3: the T+1 settlement sweep
tasks.feedback: The partner paid 99.2000 to treasury; the accrued fee clears; the clearing claim of 100.0000 is closed.

tasks.title: Entry 4: fee true-up
tasks.feedback: The extra 0.1000 is a cost and a liability.

tasks.title: Entry 9: a full refund with commission reversed
tasks.feedback: The merchant's share and our commission are reversed; 100.0000 leaves treasury.

tasks.title: Wallet after a chargeback
tasks.prompt: What is the wallet balance after the chargeback posts (allowed because the ceiling permits)?
tasks.feedback: 40 − 97 = −57. The ledger equation still holds; the merchant now owes us 57.

options.label: Treat as P1, tell your manager and Finance, never edit a number
